newsitem.title: THAILAND: Mitsubishi in aluminium joint venture in Thailand. [CORRECTED 12:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Mitsubishi in aluminium joint venture in Thailand. [CORRECTED 12:00 GMT]

text.p: Mitsubishi Aluminium will form a joint venture with Thai Maung Thong Aluminium Industry Co to produce 180 tonnes a month of aluminium extrusion products and heat exchanger components, a company executive said on Tuesday.
Peng Tuannawarat, Muang Thong's foreign department manager, told Reuters the joint venture deal would be signed on June 5.
The joint venture, to be named Muang-Max, will produce aluminium extrusion and heat exchanger components solely for automobile applications and not for the depressed construction sector, he said.
"The product will be used to make radiators and air conditioners for vehicles. It will be sold to the local automobile industry as well as exported," he added.

Thailand has become a regional hub for the automobile industry with several big names such as General Motors Co, Ford Motor Co and several Japanese makers having set up assembly plants in the country.
Thailand produced 547,317 vehicles in 1996 and the number is set to rise this year.
The Mitsubishi project, costing around 120 million baht ($4.84 million), is expected to be ready for test runa by May 1998 and will produce at full capacity in July.
Mitsubishi Aluminium will hold 50 percent stake in the project, Muang Thai Aluminium 34 percent and Mitsubishi Corp 16 percent, Peng said.
